correctness.rationale: For complex l_p² with 1<p<infinity the canonical norming functional reduces cancellation to |b|=|ar^p+d|/r^(p-1). This coercive function has range [min,infinity); after z normalization its squared minimum has derivative sign z²-(p-2)c z-(p-1) and one positive root. Applying the identical criterion to T^-1 interchanges the diagonal-modulus powers, yielding the ratio (A/D)^((p-2)/p) for c>-1. At c=-1 both thresholds vanish; all endpoint inclusions and b=0 are handled. Verified explicit p=4 complex witness and two unequal thresholds. Hilbert p=2 reciprocal-witness argument covers arbitrary invertible T. Quantitative formulas apply only to triangular T.
residual_risks: Threshold ratio not defined by division at antipodal c=-1; no isometric triangularization of arbitrary operators assumed.
